questions.question_text:
The point $P$ lies on the unit circle where the radius makes an angle of $240^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis.
Find the exact coordinates of $P$.

options.why: Swapped cosine and sine; the reference angle is $60^{\circ}$, so $\cos=\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\sin=\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
Sine is negative in the third quadrant; the $y$-value was left positive.
Cosine is negative in the third quadrant; the $x$-value was left positive.

questions.solution_text:
$P=(\cos 240^{\circ},\sin 240^{\circ})$, and $240^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+60^{\circ}$ is in the third quadrant.
$\cos 240^{\circ}=-\cos 60^{\circ}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$
$\sin 240^{\circ}=-\sin 60^{\circ}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$P=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$
